The map

Everything the project knows and does, hung on one register of concepts. Four spines: the simulated world, the supplier’s value chain, the running of the company, and how the whole thing is built. The register is small and kept by hand; every link and every gap below is generated from it at publish, from what the code and documents already say.

This is the pilot: two slices are mapped, supplier ‘Collect’ and How it’s built ‘Testing and controls’. A step in a dashed box is not on the register yet. Tap a concept to open it; its links jump across spines.

Beliefs and decisions

The data the supplier decides on: each belief is built only from what crosses the wall, feeds named decisions, and is graded against the simulation's hidden truth.

Forward cash forecast per customer

Built from bills, payments and returns, payment method, the account's record

The belief, in code company.finance.cash_forecast_provision called

Decides provision, payment plans, early warnings

Graded against the truth Gap: no grade against the world's hidden payments yet

Consumption forecast per property

Built from reads, registered consumption, weather

The belief, in code company.billing.consumption_forecast called

Decides direct debit amount, unbilled estimate, purchasing, CLV

Graded against the truth Gap: no grade against the world's true consumption yet

Can't pay versus won't pay

Built from payment history, contact record, declared circumstances

The belief, in code company.crm.affordability_inference called

Decides payment plan level, support referral, collections tone

Graded against the truth Gap: no grade against the world's hidden finances yet

Measures, one definition each

A measure carries what it counts, over whom, and the one function that computes it. The ranges a knowledge page states about the drawn world are measures too, and come from tools/world_claims.py.

  • Direct debit failure rate: counts collections returned unpaid, over collections presented in the period. Computed by Gap: no function is named as its one definition yet.
  • direct_debit_share_of_accounts, stated on gb_payment_method_migration_rates: published range 66.5% to 75.5%, checked against the drawn world by tools.world_claims._direct_debit_share_of_accounts. DESNZ Quarterly Energy Prices, Dec 2025 commentary, p.9: standard electricity DD 69% (Sept 2020) to 72% (Sept 2025), gas to 73%.

Direct debit mandate collect.mandate

The customer's instruction letting the supplier collect from their bank, which the customer can cancel at any time.

Taken from: Bacs Direct Debit scheme: Direct Debit Instruction

Also called: dd mandate, direct debit instruction, AUDDIS

Map atoms building it: W2_41_a_household_cancels_its_mandate_as_its_own_act

What the map flags

  • Crosses the wall: a cancelled mandate is not an observable the seam carries
  • 1 modules carry this concept's name and are not its declared home: company.billing.dd_mandate_register (nothing calls it)

Setting the direct debit amount collect.amount

Checks that can fail build.mutation

A check counts only once it has been seen to fail when the defect it guards is put back.

Taken from: Mutation testing literature (DeMillo, Lipton and Sayward 1978; PIT, Stryker)

Also called: mutation, neuter test

The commit gate build.gate

Dead code build.dead_code

Code nothing calls is removed or archived; it costs reading time, test time and trust.

Taken from: Fowler, Refactoring (2nd ed.): the dead-code smell

Also called: orphan, unused module, never called

What the map flags

  • rule: canon states no dead-code rule; the August orphan register keeps an uncalled module as 'unhooked'
